title: National Proper Calendars for England and for Wales (Catholic Church in England and Wales)
coverage: Complete transcription of the two National Calendar summary tables (24 Wales, 42 England celebrations) plus the E&W movable/transfer rules stated by the Liturgy Office. Diocesan propers (e.g. Cardiff-Menevia, Wrexham; English dioceses) are NOT included. 'Where no other indication is given the celebration is an optional memorial.'

Liturgy Office — Liturgical Calendar introduction: Holydays of Obligation in England and Wales; Saturday/Monday holydays transferred to Sunday (1984); Body and Blood of the Lord on Sunday (since 2006)

Liturgy Office — Calendar Notes 2024–2027 (PDF): Epiphany/Baptism, Eternal High Priest (Feast in England and Wales), St David 2 March 2026 (in Wales), St George 28 April 2025, All Souls 3 November 2025
Liturgy Office — Table of Liturgical Days / Universal Norms no. 60 (impeded solemnities are transferred)

rules.holyday_transfer: Epiphany (6 Jan), Ss Peter & Paul (29 Jun), Assumption (15 Aug), All Saints (1 Nov): if on Saturday or Monday, celebrated on the adjacent Sunday
rules.baptism: if Epiphany is kept on Sunday 7 or 8 January, the Baptism of the Lord is on the Monday after (Calendar Notes 2024)
rules.all_souls: if All Saints is moved to Sunday 2 November, All Souls is on Monday 3 November (Calendar Notes 2025)
rules.corpus_christi: Body and Blood of the Lord on the Sunday after Trinity Sunday
rules.ascension: Thursday of the 6th week of Easter (since 2017)
rules.national_solemnity: a national solemnity on a Sunday of Advent/Lent/Easter moves to the Monday; in Holy Week or the Easter Octave to the Monday after the 2nd Sunday of Easter (UNLY 60; verified: St David 2026 → 2 Mar, St George 2025 → 28 Apr)
rules.sunday: national feasts and memorials falling on a Sunday are marked impeded (Table of Liturgical Days: Sundays outrank them)
